create.name: Shelly Tygielski
create.bio:
Shelly Tygielski worked for close to twenty years as a corporate executive before making her lifelong meditation practice the centre of her working life. She has studied in the Shambhala Buddhist tradition and is trained to teach mindfulness. She began by leading a free Sunday-morning meditation on Hollywood Beach in Florida; a small circle of friends grew within two years into a community of thousands known as the Sand Tribe. Her guiding idea is that practice should carry no barrier to entry, and that inner work only finds its purpose when it reaches out into community.

In 2020 she founded Pandemic of Love, a mutual-aid network that connected people in need directly with people able to help, and in 2022 she co-founded the impact film and television company Partners in Kind. She wrote Sit Down to Rise Up, which follows the path from personal practice to collective care, and co-wrote How We Ended Racism with Justin Michael Williams. She holds a doctorate in philanthropic leadership, writes a widely read Substack, shares guided meditations on Insight Timer and gives talks on self-care as something we do together. Her Commune course, The Power of Showing Up, explores how to be present for yourself and for others.

books.title: Sit Down to Rise Up: How Radical Self-Care Can Change the World
books.author: Shelly Tygielski
books.description: Part memoir and part handbook, it traces her journey from a religious upbringing and corporate career to meditation teaching and organising. She sets out how caring for yourself can grow into caring for a community and taking part in wider change.

books.title: How We Ended Racism: Realizing a New Possibility in One Generation
books.author: Justin Michael Williams and Shelly Tygielski
books.description: Written with Justin Michael Williams, it looks back from an imagined 2050 in which racism has ended and asks what had to happen first. The authors offer practices for inner work, forgiveness and honest conversation across political divides.

courses.title: The Power of Showing Up
courses.description: A ten-day course of lessons and personal stories, about five hours in all, on turning up for yourself and the people around you with honesty, courage and purpose. A workbook with daily reflection questions is included.

free_resources.title: Guided meditations on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: Her free guided meditations on the Insight Timer app, which she links from her website for daily practice. The practices vary in style, in the spirit of her weekly beach sessions.

How We Ended Racism is co-written with Justin Michael Williams, who is already listed on Spiritpedia (justin-michael-williams): possible duplicate book entry.

Email info@shellytygielski.com is published on /contact/ as her general address and for speaking enquiries via Jill Goldberg (an assistant or agent); her literary agent's address is also listed but not used.

Her About page mentions trauma-informed practices for communities affected by gun violence, and the Sit Down to Rise Up blurb mentions healing from chronic health issues as biography; neither is used in the bio or descriptions. Book kept: it promises no treatment.
Insight Timer free resource uses the insig.ht short link from her own site; the Insight Timer profile page is a script-rendered app page whose content couldn't be checked with curl.

Her own YouTube channel has only two videos (12 subscribers); the other videos are on Mindful, New World Library and Garrison Institute channels, where she is the main speaker. The Garrison book event is a conversation with Sharon Salzberg.
